statement: Whole-node teardown terminates every request/call cell worker: a stop-all chain (bootstrap seed/join cleanup -> ServiceRuntimeLifecycle.shutdown -> WasmComponentDriver.shutdown -> WasiComponentCellRuntime.shutdown -> worker.terminate) replaces the absent per-replica stop path at shutdown, so the call-binding-account-summary example runner exits naturally with zero live handles and its bounded-exit workaround (the SHUTDOWN_BOUND_MS Promise.race and the explicit process.exit) is deleted. Successor of the exhausted managed-split-shutdown-timer-leak quest: its measured matrix proved the runner hang is caused by untorn-down cell Workers (3 MessagePorts, reproducible with NO split), not by split timers. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/node-shutdown-cell-worker-teardown.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — cell-runtime-stop-all, driver-stop-all, lifecycle-dispatch, seed-cleanup-wiring, join-cleanup-wiring, and runner-natural-exit receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The stop-all lives at the runtime owner boundary (WasiComponentCellRuntime owns its cells map; WasmComponentDriver owns its bookkeeping; ServiceRuntimeLifecycle dispatches to drivers by capability, never by runtime-kind branch). Bootstrap cleanup handlers only INVOKE the chain; they do not enumerate cells or workers themselves.
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding stop-all/dispatch/wiring link is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert checks) at quest terminal; no hand-authored metric values.
